llm_grading.feedback: The component demonstrates strong overall quality. Readability is high: the file is divided into clearly commented sections (Types, Constants, Worklet helpers, Sub-components, Error Boundary, Main Component, Styles), naming is descriptive, and TypeScript interfaces are well-structured. Architecture separates gesture handling cleanly with Gesture.Pinch and Gesture.Pan running simultaneously via simultaneousWithExternalGesture and withRef cross-references; the StationDot and StationBottomSheet sub-components are properly extracted and memoised. The bottom sheet animation is isolated in its own Animated.View with its own useSharedValue. A minor architecture concern is the transformOrigin hack (set as 'left center' cast to undefined) for line segment rotation, which means segments rotate around their center rather than start point — a visual inaccuracy but not a crash risk. Maintainability is good: worklet helpers clampWorklet and computePanBoundsWorklet are standalone functions at module level, clearly marked with 'worklet' directive and containing no runOnJS calls, which correctly avoids JS thread blocking. The test file covers smoke testing, accessibility labels, press callbacks, bottom sheet lifecycle, error handling (null detail), and edge cases (empty stations/segments). Performance is well-addressed: all transform computations happen in onUpdate/onEnd gesture callbacks running on the UI thread via worklets; the station overlay uses useMemo to avoid regenerating all station elements on every JS frame; React.memo is applied to StationDot and StationBottomSheet; useCallback guards all event handlers. Security is clean: no hardcoded credentials, all external data accessed through typed props, null guards on optional fields (detail.exits !== undefined, detail.address !== undefined), error boundary catches unexpected rendering errors, and the detail request uses .catch() to suppress promise rejections gracefully. The component would benefit from: (1) fixing the transformOrigin line segment rotation, (2) adding a proper withRef-based simultaneousHandlers pattern that matches gesture-handler v2 API more idiomatically, (3) debouncing syncToJS calls during fast pinch/pan to reduce JS bridge traffic.

feedback: PASS with score 0.91. All 9 code checks passed (1.0). The InteractiveRouteMap component correctly implements simultaneousHandlers for pinch+pan, uses useSharedValue/useAnimatedStyle for 60fps animation, marks all worklet functions with the 'worklet' directive, applies React.memo/useMemo/useCallback memoization, includes a RouteMapErrorBoundary error boundary with friendly fallback UI, and provides comprehensive accessibilityLabel coverage on all touch targets. TypeScript strict mode is maintained with no 'any' types, path aliases are used throughout, and no colors are hardcoded.
